subject: Private deployment kickoff — network segmentation, nodeclasses, and storage clarifications
messages:
From: Diane Park <diane.park@maplecityhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Maple City Health Ops <ops@maplecityhealth.com>, Tam Nguyen <tam.nguyen@maplecityhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment kickoff — network/VLAN and nodeclass questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for agreeing to help with our private deployment planning. We are beginning procurement and need to validate a few architecture constraints before we lock hardware and network. High-level info attached (site-inventory.csv). Quick asks below so we can confirm next-week timelines: 

- Node classes: we expect to have two tenant types — inference-heavy (4xA100 equiv) and control/ingest (4 CPU nodes). Can you confirm recommended node counts per availability zone for an initial 3-AZ footprint?
- Storage: we plan to use a SAN-backed block store (iSCSI) + local NVMe on inference nodes for cache. Are there specific requirements for Kubernetes CSI (LVM vs external-CSI) or recommended IOPS for model artifacts?
- Network: our infra team requires suggested VLAN segregation (management, control plane, inference, monitoring) and MTU recommendations for NIC bonding. Any constraints for egress NAT/peering with our analytics VPC?
- Security & compliance: we need a short checklist on key management (KMS/HSM) integration for model artifact encryption, audit log retention, and whether Redwood supports an air-gapped private bundle for onboarding.

Can we schedule a 45-min call next Tuesday or Wednesday morning PST to walk through these? Procurement deadlines: PO requested by 2026-02-20.

Appreciate it —
Diane
Director, Infrastructure
Maple City Health

--
Attachment: site-inventory.csv (columns: rack_id, mgmt_vlan, public_ip_block, onsite_k8s_engineer_contact)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Diane Park <diane.park@maplecityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff — network/VLAN and nodeclass questions

Diane —

Thanks for the details and the inventory CSV. I added Marissa (platform ops lead) and Karthik (solutions/infra) to help with sizing and storage guidance. Attached is our Redwood Private intake checklist (redwood-private-checklist.xlsx) — please fill the left column items if possible before the call; it speeds prep.

Preliminary answers inline:
- Node counts: for a 3-AZ footprint we typically recommend (per AZ) 2 control-plane replicas (HA) + 3-4 inference GPU nodes and 2-3 CPU ingress/queue nodes to start. That gives room for rolling upgrades and a single-AZ failure. Exact numbers depend on concurrency targets — can you provide expected concurrent requests/sec and peak tokens/sec?
- Storage: SAN block store for persistent PVs is fine. For model artifacts we recommend a fast block class (differing from the archival class) with at least 10k read IOPS per inference node for low-latency loads; local NVMe should be used as ephemeral KV/prefix cache only (no long-term state). We support CSI drivers including LVM-CSI and external CSI; we typically deploy a CSI LVM layer on top of local NVMe for ephemeral caching when customers want tighter control.
- Network segregation: recommended VLANs: 10 (management), 20 (control plane), 30 (inference), 40 (monitoring/logging). MTU: 9000 where SAN and switches support jumbo frames; fallback 1500. Egress: we can NAT through your analytics VPC but prefer a routed peer with firewall rules for reduced NAT hairpin latency.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer KMS with envelope encryption; HSM-backed keys are supported via standard KMIP or cloud KMS integrations. For air-gapped installs we provide a private bundle; some redaction of telemetry is configurable.

Next steps: can Marissa/Karthik and I get the concurrency numbers and the infra engineer contact? We'll prepare a short network sketch before the call. Proposed times: Tue 2026-02-10 09:30-10:15 PST or Wed 2026-02-11 09:00-09:45 PST.

Best,
Sofia
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-checklist.xlsx (deployment intake template)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff — network/VLAN and nodeclass questions

On Mon, Feb 9, 2026 at 10:04 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
> Diane —
> 
> Thanks for the details...

Adding a few implementation-focused notes for Diane and your infra team so procurement includes the right SKUs:

- Node sizing guidance (quick):
  * Inference GPU pool: 3x A100-equivalent per AZ to start (we treat each GPU node as a single pod-sched unit for large-model serving); plan for one spare host per AZ to absorb failover.
  * Control plane / k8s masters: small dedicated VMs (4 vCPU / 16GB) on a management VLAN — 3 nodes for quorum.
  * Ingest/ETL nodes: CPU-heavy r5-like nodes, suggested 2 per AZ for resiliency.

- Storage classes:
  * model-artifacts-class (fast block): backed by SAN with multipath; recommend 250 MB/s sustained per inference node for warm model pulls (actual depends on model shard sizes).
  * archive-class: cheaper SATA array for logs / durable artifacts; snapshots to offsite for disaster recovery.
  * ephemeral-cache: local NVMe (no replication) for KV cache. Use LVM-CSI if you want per-tenant quotas on local NVMe.

- Kubernetes considerations:
  * Taints/tolerations to isolate GPU workloads.
  * Pod topology spread to keep GPU pods across hosts.
  * Node eviction policy tuned to prefer draining CPU nodes before GPU nodes.

- Network specifics:
  * Separate management plane with restricted SSH and a bastion.
  * Control-plane API should be reachable only from mgmt and Redwood monitoring addresses (we'll provide IPs).
  * If you require private registry mirroring, we can provide a registry bundle and recommended sync schedule.

I'll draft a one-page network sketch (VLANs, control-plane endpoints, egress path) and drop it into the Drive link before the call. Also need an infra contact for switch/VLAN configuration.

-M
Marissa Cole
Platform Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: network-segmentation-sketch.pdf

Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff — network/VLAN and nodeclass questions

Sofia / Marissa —

Thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side (procurement & compliance):

- Concurrency: we expect ~120 concurrent inference requests during peak with median request size ~600 tokens; peak tokens/sec ~18k.
- Throughput: we can guarantee 12 Gbps per rack to the SAN; local NVMe will be 2x 3.2TB NVMe per GPU host.
- Backups/snapshots: procurement team asks how often Redwood recommends snapshots of model-artifacts-class. We prefer daily snapshots with a 30-day retention.
- SOC2 / evidence: I'll attach our procurement timeline (procurement-timeline.pdf). We will need SOC2 artifact pointers (controls around access logs, encryption at rest) during the contract review. Can Redwood provide a short SOC2 evidence checklist?

We can host the call Wed 2026-02-11 09:00 PST — Tam (ops) will join to discuss VLANs.

Thanks —
Diane

Diane —

Great — Wed 2026-02-11 09:00 PST is confirmed on our calendar (invite sent). Quick answers ahead of the call so your procurement has what they need: 

- Snapshots: daily snapshots for model-artifacts-class with 30-day retention is our recommended default and aligns with typical deployments. We can also support hourly short-term snapshots for critical model rollouts during canary windows.
- SOC2 evidence: we'll provide a SOC2 evidence bundle (controls mapping, access log samples, encryption key management design) as part of the enterprise review. I'll coordinate with our security/compliance team and send a checklist and timeframe by EOD Monday.

Action items before the call:
1) Diane / Tam: fill the redwood-private-checklist.xlsx items for rack IPs, switch VLAN ranges, and concurrence SLA targets.
2) Redwood: Marissa / Karthik / I to produce the network sketch and a short SOC2 evidence checklist.

Thanks, looking forward to the call tomorrow.

Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
